correctness.rationale: A geometric orbit-barycenter triangulation holds for finite simplicial actions. For a wheel under a nonidentity rotation, no spoke orbit is admissible and rim-edge orbit conflict is empty/K2/C_g according to gcd(n,a); for odd rim reflection, the fixed spoke is an isolated conflict vertex and the others form P_m; for even rim reflections, the two distinct axis cases give K2 plus P_(m-2) or P_(m+1). These are exact PL identifications and cover n>=5 including boundaries. Graph independence join/suspension and the established path/cycle formulas imply all homotopy types. A pure-Python standalone checker independently passed 4080 nonidentity orbit graph templates, 105 full invariant-face comparisons and 28 mod-two homology tests; finite tests were not used to prove all widths. Remaining risk is lack of independent mathematical audit.

originality.rationale: The nearest fully inspected primary treatment provides ordinary wheel matching-complex nonequivariant homotopy and cycle-independence homotopy; neither determines any nonidentity geometric fixed subspace. Indexed records on wheel Morse complexes concern acyclic Hasse-matchings, not edge matchings; indexed cycle matching characters concern a different graph/invariant. Statement and implication comparisons show no prior result found asserting the simultaneous explicit PL fixed-space types for rotations and both reflection classes. Unindexed equivalent research remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The natural equivariant refinement of the known wheel matching-complex classification resolves all nontrivial standard dihedral fixed-point spaces across infinitely many wheel widths, with explicit PL orbit models; it yields empty fixed loci, contractible loci, unbounded sphere dimensions and two-sphere bouquets, and detects geometric information not implied by rational traces, nonequivariant Betti numbers, or the prior graph-family results. This is a complete motivated structural classification, not a numerical arbitrary slice or routine renaming.
